from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Introduction: What is a Vector?", [

        # Initialize objects
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 6, 1], y_range=[0, 4, 1], axis_config={"include_numbers": False}).scale(0.5)

        vector = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=axes.c2p(3, 2), color=WHITE, buff=0)
        label = MathTex(r"\vec{v}").next_to(vector.get_center(), UP)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(axes), Create(vector), Write(label))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Indicate(vector, color="#FF5733"))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF5733")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===

        self.play(FadeIn(mag_line))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#33FF57")
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Vector Addition: The Head-to-Tail Rule", [
            "Vectors add by head-to-tail placement.",
            "Place the second vector's tail at the head.",
            "The resultant is the total displacement."
        ])
        
        # Define vectors
        u = Vector([1.5, 1, 0], color=WHITE)
        v = Vector([1, -1.5, 0], color=WHITE)
        u_label = MathTex(r"\vec{u}", color=WHITE).next_to(u.get_center(), UP)
        v_label = MathTex(r"\vec{v}", color=WHITE).next_to(v.get_center(), UP)
        
        # Initial positions
        self.place_at_grid(u, "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(u_label, "A2")
        self.place_at_grid(v, "D2")
        self.place_at_grid(v_label, "C2")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Create(u), Create(u_label), Create(v), Create(v_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        # Shift v to start at the head of u
        target_pos = u.get_end()
        self.play(
            v.animate.shift(target_pos - v.get_start()),
            v_label.animate.shift(target_pos - v.get_start())
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        # Resultant vector
        resultant = Vector(u.get_vector() + v.get_vector(), color=GREEN)
        resultant.move_to(u.get_start() + (u.get_vector() + v.get_vector()) / 2)
        res_label = MathTex(r"\vec{u}+\vec{v}", color=GREEN).next_to(resultant.get_center(), RIGHT)
        
        self.play(Create(resultant), Write(res_label))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Scalar Multiplication", [
            "Scalars change a vector's length or direction.",
            "Multiplying by a scalar scales the vector.",
            "Negative scalars reverse the vector's direction."
        ])
        
        # Vector Setup
        origin = ORIGIN
        v_coords = np.array([1, 1, 0])
        vector = Arrow(origin, v_coords, color=WHITE)
        label_v = MathTex(r"\vec{v}").next_to(vector.get_end(), UP)
        
        v_group = VGroup(vector, label_v)
        self.place_at_grid(v_group, 'C3')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(vector), Write(label_v))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        v2 = Arrow(origin, 2 * v_coords, color="#FFFF00")
        label_2v = MathTex(r"2\vec{v}").next_to(v2.get_end(), UP)
        v2_group = VGroup(v2, label_2v)
        self.place_at_grid(v2_group, 'C3')
        
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(vector.copy(), v2), Write(label_2v))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        v_neg = Arrow(origin, -1 * v_coords, color="#FF00FF")
        label_neg_v = MathTex(r"-\vec{v}").next_to(v_neg.get_end(), DOWN)
        v_neg_group = VGroup(v_neg, label_neg_v)
        self.place_at_grid(v_neg_group, 'C3')
        
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(vector.copy(), v_neg), Write(label_neg_v))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Basis vectors i and j are building blocks.",
            "They span the 2D coordinate system.",
            "Any vector is their linear combination."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Basis Vectors: The Building Blocks", lecture_lines)
        
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-1, 3], y_range=[-1, 3], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.5)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A2", "F5")
        
        i_vec = Vector([1, 0], color=YELLOW)
        j_vec = Vector([0, 1], color=BLUE)
        
        origin = axes.c2p(0, 0)
        i_vec.shift(origin - i_vec.get_start())
        j_vec.shift(origin - j_vec.get_start())
        
        i_label = MathTex(r"\hat{i}", color=YELLOW).next_to(axes.c2p(1, 0), DR, buff=0.1)
        j_label = MathTex(r"\hat{j}", color=BLUE).next_to(axes.c2p(0, 1), UP, buff=0.1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(axes))
        self.play(GrowArrow(i_vec), Write(i_label))
        self.play(GrowArrow(j_vec), Write(j_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        grid = NumberPlane(x_range=[-1, 3], y_range=[-1, 3]).scale(0.5).move_to(axes.get_center())
        self.play(FadeIn(grid))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        target_vec = Vector([2, 1], color=GREEN)
        target_vec.shift(origin - target_vec.get_start())
        target_label = MathTex(r"2\hat{i} + 1\hat{j}", color=GREEN).next_to(axes.c2p(2, 1), UR, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(GrowArrow(target_vec), Write(target_label))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Application and Conclusion", [
            "Vectors are essential in computer graphics.",
            "They model physical forces in physics.",
            "Magnitude, direction, and combinations are key."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        vector_a = Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT * 1.5 + UP * 1.0, color=BLUE).shift(self.grid["C3"])
        vector_b = Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT * 1.0 + DOWN * 1.0, color=YELLOW).shift(self.grid["C3"])
        label_a = Text("Thrust", font_size=20, color=BLUE).next_to(vector_a.get_end(), UP)
        label_b = Text("Wind", font_size=20, color=YELLOW).next_to(vector_b.get_end(), DOWN)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.play(Create(vector_a), Write(label_a))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF00FF")
        self.play(Create(vector_b), Write(label_b))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        combined_vec = Arrow(ORIGIN, vector_a.get_vector() + vector_b.get_vector(), color="#00FFFF").shift(self.grid["C3"])
        self.play(Create(combined_vec))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(VGroup(vector_a, vector_b, combined_vec, label_a, label_b)))

outline.topic: Fundamentals of Linear Algebra: Understanding Vectors

sections.title: Introduction: What is a Vector?
sections.content: Define a vector not just as a list of numbers, but as a directed arrow representing a move in space (magnitude and direction). Contrast scalars (single values) with vectors (multi-dimensional components).
sections.example: Visualizing a 'Player Character' on a 2D game map moving 3 units right and 2 units up, represented as vector [3, 2].

sections.title: Vector Addition: The Head-to-Tail Rule
sections.content: Explain vector addition geometrically. Demonstrate placing the tail of the second vector at the head of the first. Introduce the concept of the 'Resultant' vector.
sections.example: A cat chasing a butterfly: Vector A is the cat's initial movement, Vector B is the butterfly's sudden turn. The resultant shows the cat's total displacement.

sections.title: Scalar Multiplication: Scaling the Arrow
sections.content: Explain how multiplying a vector by a scalar changes its length (stretching or shrinking) or reverses its direction (negative scalars).
sections.example: A 'Zoom' function on a smartphone map: scaling the displacement vector [1, 1] by 3 results in [3, 3], effectively moving the view further away from the origin.

sections.title: Basis Vectors: The Building Blocks
sections.content: Introduce 'i' [1, 0] and 'j' [0, 1] as the foundation of the 2D coordinate system. Explain that any vector is just a linear combination of these basis vectors.
sections.example: Using Lego bricks (basis) to build a wall; regardless of the shape, every complex structure (vector) is built from these standard unit blocks.

sections.title: Application and Conclusion
sections.content: Briefly connect vectors to modern applications like Computer Graphics (transforming shapes) and Physics (force vectors). Recap the core concepts: Magnitude, Direction, and Linear Combination.
sections.example: A drone flight controller calculating wind resistance (Vector A) vs. motor thrust (Vector B) to maintain a steady hover.
